chunks: And that which Muhammad al-Halabi narrated: that he asked him about the oil of henna and the oil of violet, 'Do we anoint ourselves with it when we intend to enter the state of Ihram?' So he said:

'Yes.' This does not contradict what we mentioned, because it is permissible that the permission for that applies if one knows that its scent will disappear at the time of Ihram, or that it is in a state of necessity from which there is no escape to anything else. It is also permissible that the intended meaning is when the violet oil is of that type from which the pleasant scent has already departed, at which point it follows the ruling of Shayraj. That which indicates this is what was narrated:

key_terms.إِحْرَام: State of ritual consecration for Hajj or Umrah
key_terms.الشَّيْرَج: A type of musk or scent used as a benchmark for permissible scent in Ihram

ai.seo_question: Can a pilgrim use scented oil before entering Ihram?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi records this narration from Muhammad al-Halabi to resolve apparent contradictions regarding scented oils in Ihram by offering three scholarly interpretations: the scent dissipates before Ihram commences, it is used out of necessity, or the specific oil has lost its fragrance. This highlights the Shia juristic principle of distinguishing between the substance itself and its lingering scent, ensuring that minor perfumes do not invalidate the sacred state when conditions are met.
